sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others Counsel for Applicant :- Om Prakash Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
Sri Ravi Sahu, Advocate has filed vakalatnama on behalf of informant, which is taken on record.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant-accused, learned counsel for the informant, learned A.G.A.
for the State and perused the record.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant-accused in case crime No.225 of 2022,
under Section 363, 366, 376 IPC and section 5/6 POCSO Act, police station Punchh, District Jhansi with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.
It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant-accused that the applicant-accused is innocent and he has not committed any offence.
Alleged incident has been shown of 11.11.2022 but first information report has been lodged on 17.11.2022.
It was alleged in the FIR that applicant-accused has enticed away the minor daughter of informant.

In her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim girl has stated that she is a student of B.Sc. first year and she was in love with applicant and she wanted to marry with applicant but her family members were marrying Kuldeep vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194786844/
1 her with some other person and thus, on 11.11.2022 she has gone with applicant to Pune with her own free will.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., victim has stated that her family members were not ready for her marriage with applicant and thus, she has gone with applicant to Pune with her own free will.
In her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she has further stated that she wants to live with applicant and she does not want to go with her parents.
She has also stated that she is having pregnancy of two months.

Learned counsel submitted that as per school record,
the age of victim girl is 17 years but in fact she is a major girl and they both wanted to marry with each other but before they could marry, they were apprehended by the police.
Learned counsel submitted that applicant as well as victim wants to marry with each other and as applicant is in jail thus, marriage could not place so far.
It was stated that as soon as applicant's gets bail, he would marry with victim girl.

Lastly, it has been submitted that the applicant-accused is languishing in jail since 16.12.2022, having no criminal history, and that in case the applicant-accused is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in trial.

Learned counsel for the informant has not opposed the bail and submitted that as victim is having pregnancy with relations from applicant and that they both are ready to marry with each other, thus,
bail application of applicant is not opposed and the applicant may be granted bail, so that he may marry with victim girl.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail.

Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of custody and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

Let the applicant-accused Kuldeep involved in aforesaid crime be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:
1. The applicant-accused shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
2. The applicant-accused shall not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
3. The applicant-accused shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
4. The applicant-accused shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

5. The applicant-accused shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
